records.claim: The exemption that covers a domestic driveway hard surface is Class 6 of Schedule 2, Part 1 to the Planning and Development Regulations 2001, as substituted in full by Article 6 of S.I. No. 454 of 2011.
records.authority: Office of the Attorney General (Irish Statute Book)
records.source_title: S.I. No. 454/2011 - Planning and Development (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2011
recheck_triggers: A new Exempted Development instrument is made.
Any instrument amends S.I. No. 600 of 2001, Schedule 2, Part 1, Class 6.
A relevant published Irish planning determination comes to light.
prohibited_readings: Any statement of the pre-2011 vehicle-count condition as current law.
records.notes: Gate 3C enumerated every Planning and Development Regulations instrument 2002-2026 from the Irish Statute Book year indexes and scanned each for 'Class 6' on a word boundary, 'hard surface' and 'motor vehicles'. S.I. 454/2011 is the only instrument that substituted Part 1 Class 6. S.I. 649/2025 matches 'Class 6' but inserts Class 6A of PART 3 (agricultural slurry storage) and does not touch Part 1. The repealed vehicle-count condition has not been law since 13 September 2011.

records.claim: Current Class 6(b)(ii) exempts the provision of a hard surface in the area of the garden forward of the front building line of the house, or to the side of the side building line, for purposes incidental to the enjoyment of the house as such. Where that hard surface is 25 square metres or greater, or comprises more than 50 per cent of that part of the garden, whichever is the smaller, it must be constructed using permeable materials or otherwise allow rainwater to soak into the ground.

value.test: incidental to the enjoyment of the house as such
locations: forward of the front building line
to the side of the side building line
value.condition_above_threshold: permeable materials, or otherwise allow rainwater to soak into the ground

records.notes: vehicle_count_limit is null because the substituted Class 6 contains no vehicle count, NOT because vehicle numbers are unconstrained. The incidental test survives, and conditions attached to an individual property can still bite.

records.claim: Rent-a-Room Relief applies to income received for the use of a room or rooms in a qualifying residence, let as residential accommodation.

value.scope: a room or rooms in a qualifying residence

records.source_title: Rent-a-Room Relief - What conditions must be met?
records.notes: PlotNua states Revenue's SCOPE and lets the scope carry the conclusion. Revenue has not published a sentence saying the relief does not apply to a parking space, and PlotNua does not attribute one to them. A parking space is not a room and is not residential accommodation; that is why the relief does not reach driveway income.

records.claim: The annual Rent-a-Room Relief exemption limit is EUR 14,000, applied to gross income before expenses. If gross income exceeds the limit, the total amount is taxed.
records.source_title: Rent-a-Room Relief - What conditions must be met?
records.notes: Carried so PlotNua can correct the common belief that this allowance covers driveway income. It is a published statutory scheme threshold, not an earnings figure, and it is never applied to a homeowner's own numbers.

records.claim: Where gross rental income does not exceed the Rent-a-Room exemption limit, it is not liable to Income Tax, PRSI or USC.

value.condition: gross income at or below the exemption limit

records.source_title: Rent-a-Room Relief - What conditions must be met?
records.notes: Held to make the contrast exact: the relief a homeowner is thinking of is genuinely generous, and genuinely does not reach a driveway.

records.claim: Under the Consumer Insurance Contracts Act 2019 a consumer's pre-contractual duty of disclosure is confined to providing responses to the questions the insurer asks, answered honestly and with reasonable care. The consumer is under no duty to volunteer information beyond those questions.

value.replaces: uberrima fides at the pre-contractual stage

records.authority: Office of the Attorney General (Irish Statute Book)
records.notes: States the PRE-CONTRACTUAL position only. It does not say a homeowner need tell their insurer nothing, and it must never be presented that way. Section 15 governs the position during the contract and is carried separately.

records.claim: Where a consumer has answered the insurer's questions honestly and with reasonable care, an innocent misrepresentation does not entitle the insurer to avoid the contract and the claim must be paid. A negligent misrepresentation attracts a compensatory and proportionate remedy.
records.authority: Office of the Attorney General (Irish Statute Book)
prohibited_readings: Presentation to a homeowner in any form.
Any suggestion that an inaccurate answer to an insurer carries no consequence.
records.notes: homeowner_safe is FALSE on purpose. The remedy ladder is accurate and useful to PlotNua's reasoning, but presenting it to a homeowner invites them to work out how wrong an answer they could give and still be paid. It informs what PlotNua will not say; it is not itself said.
